title: Bound orbits increase ballistic core energy gains by up to 2.4 times in a 108-day model
abstract: Can a parabolic model of core formation describe positive energy shifts in a repeating partial disruption on a bound orbit? We extend a ballistic line-density model with first and second orbit variations. For a 108.44-day Newtonian orbit around a 1e7-solar-mass black hole, four one-solar-mass test stars give bound-to-parabolic energy ratios of 1.07-1.13 at 5 days, 1.36-1.44 at 20 days and 2.27-2.35 at 50 days. A five-solar-radius case with beta = 2 and alpha = 18.4 needs core formation at 10.07 days for an isolated positive period change of 0.3 day. Finite differences and direct density-peak calculations check the method. This is a conditional model result, not a measured core formation time or an explanation of the ASASSN-14ko stall. Core formation, stellar survival and relativistic effects require further tests. Code, model outputs, provenance and a source retrieval script are included.

display.caption: Bound and parabolic ballistic energy shifts at fixed pericentre and formation time. Solid period-change curves use bound orbits; dotted curves use parabolic orbits. These are prescribed models, not fits to flare data.
